name: Community — MiniMax H3 (Sol-Attn + EasyCache)
author: kijai
description: MiniMax H3 video with Sol-Attn (arXiv 2607.24027, training-free sparse attention) stacked with EasyCache (native ComfyUI step-skipping cache) — full 20-step quality, no LoRA, no step reduction. Tested T2V at 5s/480p/20 steps: Sol-Attn alone ran 2m43s; adding EasyCache (reuse_threshold 0.3) dropped that to 115.0s with 7/20 steps skipped (1.54x on top of Sol-Attn) — faster than either technique alone, with no visible quality loss across sampled frames. Sol-Attn and EasyCache patch the model at different layers (EasyCache wraps via ComfyUI's WrappersMP system, Sol-Attn patches diffusion_model.blocks directly), so they stack cleanly. Early/experimental: the Sol-Attn node repo is brand new and explicitly marked experimental by its own author. Only became testable once SimpliGen 1.43.x added the Python dev headers Sol-Attn's Triton kernels need to compile. REQUIRES SimpliGen Settings > Advanced > 'Faster Attention' to be ON. As of SimpliGen 1.44.2, this setting defaults OFF, and when it is off SimpliGen actively uninstalls the triton-windows pip package from the engine's Python on every startup. Sol-Attn hard-imports triton at load time, so the custom node fails to import ('No module named triton') and the preset cannot generate - SimpliGen's own 'Repair now' prompt will NOT fix this, since the node itself is not broken or out of date; only re-enabling Faster Attention restores triton. This still holds on SimpliGen 1.46.0, which added detection and repair of half-installed custom nodes: that targets incomplete installs, and this node is complete - it ships no requirements.txt, pyproject.toml or install script at all, so there is no declared dependency for a repair to reinstall. The missing package belongs to SimpliGen's Faster Attention setting, not to the node.

presets.name: MiniMax H3 Text to Video (Sol-Attn + EasyCache)
presets.description: Describe a scene and get video with matching stereo sound. Uses Sol-Attn sparse attention instead of (or alongside - unconfirmed) SimpliGen's built-in automatic SageAttention. Experimental - the node is brand new and its interaction with SimpliGen's automatic SageAttention hasn't been characterized. Stacked with EasyCache step-skipping for extra speed on top of Sol-Attn (tested: 115.0s vs 2m43s for Sol-Attn alone on T2V, 7/20 steps skipped) - no visible quality loss.
presets.tagline: MiniMax H3 T2V with sparse Sol-Attn + EasyCache - experimental

This still holds on SimpliGen 1.46.0, which added detection and repair of half-installed custom nodes: that targets incomplete installs, and this node is complete - it ships no requirements.txt, pyproject.toml or install script at all, so there is no declared dependency for a repair to reinstall. The missing package belongs to SimpliGen's Faster Attention setting, not to the node.

requirements.notes: Same base weights as SimpliGen's official MiniMax H3 pack - no new downloads. Needs the ComfyUI-SolAttn_triton custom node, which itself needs Triton's JIT compiler working (requires Python.h/python3XX.lib in the engine's Python - present from SimpliGen 1.43.x). Sol-Attn is brand new and experimental; its interaction with SimpliGen's automatic SageAttention has not been characterized. EasyCache is native to ComfyUI, no extra custom node beyond Sol-Attn's. REQUIRES SimpliGen Settings > Advanced > 'Faster Attention' to be ON. As of SimpliGen 1.44.2, this setting defaults OFF, and when it is off SimpliGen actively uninstalls the triton-windows pip package from the engine's Python on every startup. Sol-Attn hard-imports triton at load time, so the custom node fails to import ('No module named triton') and the preset cannot generate - SimpliGen's own 'Repair now' prompt will NOT fix this, since the node itself is not broken or out of date; only re-enabling Faster Attention restores triton. This still holds on SimpliGen 1.46.0, which added detection and repair of half-installed custom nodes: that targets incomplete installs, and this node is complete - it ships no requirements.txt, pyproject.toml or install script at all, so there is no declared dependency for a repair to reinstall. The missing package belongs to SimpliGen's Faster Attention setting, not to the node. RAM requirement verified downward: every preset in this pack has been run repeatedly on a 32GB machine (31.2GB usable) with a 12GB RTX 4070 Ti, so the earlier 48GB figure was too conservative. The engine streams model weights rather than holding them resident, which is what makes a ~20GB checkpoint workable well under its own size. 16GB has not been tested.

presets.name: MiniMax H3 Reference to Video (Sol-Attn + EasyCache)
presets.description: Carry a character and a look across into a new scene, with sound. Uses Sol-Attn sparse attention instead of (or alongside - unconfirmed) SimpliGen's built-in automatic SageAttention; no LoRA, no step reduction (still 20 steps, same as the official R2V preset). Experimental - the node is brand new and its interaction with SimpliGen's automatic SageAttention hasn't been characterized. Reference-video conditioning is much heavier than plain text conditioning (confirmed elsewhere in this repo: the official R2V preset ran ~290s/step vs ~10-20s/step for T2V on the same hardware). Stacked with EasyCache step-skipping for extra speed on top of Sol-Attn (tested: 115.0s vs 2m43s for Sol-Attn alone on T2V, 7/20 steps skipped) - no visible quality loss.
presets.tagline: Reference images/video steer the cast and style + EasyCache - experimental
